 CT launches Mobile ID: your official state i.d. on your phone
 The display for the Connecticut Mobile ID app on the App Store.
 App Store
 dt_original: None
 show_updated: None
 ---
 By Dave Mager Nov 17, 2026, 05:22 PM ET Local wtic News Go Deeper 
 Gampel family sues UConn over renaming Gampel Pavilion
 Stamford police officer facing charges
 NEWINGTON (WTIC News) -- By installing a new program that goes live on Wednesday, you can now carry your official Connecticut identification on your phone, according to Gov. Ned Lamont, the Department of Motor Vehicles and the Department of Consumer Protection.
 It’s called the Connecticut Mobile ID app, which can found on the App Store or Google Play. If you download the app and upload your basic information and a selfie, the app will match your data with state records. It then produces a QR code each time you need to verify your identification.
 State officials say it can be used at TSA security checkpoints plus bars, restaurants and other outlets that carry a “verifier” that can swipe the QR code that carries your i.d.
 “It’ll come up ‘green’ on the screen, which means it’s a real i.d.,” explains Phil Barnett, owner of the Hartford Restaurant Group, whose Wood-n-Tap restaurants are taking part in the program. “If it comes up ‘red,’ then it’s a false i.d. The best part about it is that it will show their age, so you’ll know if they are eligible to drink alcoholic beverages.” 
 Connecticut Mobile ID is not accepted by law enforcement, so you’ll still need your physical driver’s license if you get pulled over.
 But state officials attending a rollout event at Wood-n-Tap Newington believe the convenience of swiping their phone in other situations when i.d. is required will win over residents.
 “The conveniency of having it on your phone… We’ve all gone through airports, right?” says DMV Commissioner Tony Guerrera. “The next thing you gotta pull out your license… you put your travel bag down, you’re pulling out your license, you gotta grab it. Now, all you do is, boom (swipe your phone) and walk right through.”
 “It gives residents another secure way to show their i.d.” says Consumer Protection Commissioner Bryan Caffarelli. “We’re helping the businesses that we regulate learn and understand how to accept it confidently, responsibly and in compliance with the law.”
 “We’re just trying to make our government a little more responsive,” said Gov. Lamont at a rollout event at Wood-n-Tap Newington. “These little things show we’re making a difference, making your lives a little bit easier.”
